knowledge.content: Task: Transform /app/input.csv to match /app/expected.csv using Vim macros. Output: /app/apply_macros.vim
Macro constraints: Must use registers a, b, c. All three must be non-empty. Total keystrokes < 200 across all macros or risk timeout.
Allowed commands in apply_macros.vim: call setreg('a/b/c', "keystrokes"), :%normal! @a/@b/@c, :wq or :x. NO Vimscript functions, shell escapes, or scripting languages.
Macro content: Can use basic Vim keystrokes and essential Ex commands (e.g., :s/ for search/replace). Each setreg call must be single line, no linebreaks.
Test command: vim -Nu NONE -n -Es /app/input.csv -S /app/apply_macros.vim. Must run headlessly and exit 0.
Success criteria: (1) apply_macros.vim exists with only allowed commands, (2) Vim exits 0, (3) input.csv matches expected.csv byte-for-byte after transformation.

Transformation pattern identified: Input has 3 CSV columns with mixed-case words and spaces (e.g., " alpha1 , BeTa1 , GaMmA1 "). Output reverses column order, uppercases all text, removes spaces, changes delimiter from comma to semicolon, and appends ";OK" (e.g., "GAMMA1;BETA1;ALPHA1;OK").
Input format: Each line has pattern "  word1  ,  word2  ,  word3  " with variable spacing and mixed case. Output format: "WORD3;WORD2;WORD1;OK" (uppercase, no spaces, semicolon delimiter, OK suffix).

procedural.content: Step 3: Created apply_macros.vim with approach: macro 'a' uses :s/\s*\(\w\+\)\s*,\s*\(\w\+\)\s*,\s*\(\w\+\)\s*/\3;\2;\1/ to reverse columns and change delimiters while stripping whitespace; macro 'b' uses :s/.*/\U&/ to uppercase entire line; macro 'c' uses :s/$/;OK/ to append suffix. Each macro includes \r (carriage return) to execute the Ex command. Total approach relies on three sequential :%normal! calls.

Step 4: Agent adopted incremental testing approach - created test_input.csv with 5 sample lines before running on full 1M row dataset. This validates macro correctness and prevents wasting time on full file if script has bugs. Smart practice for large file transformations.

Step 5: Test validation confirmed macro script correctness. Running vim -Nu NONE -n -Es test_input.csv -S apply_macros.vim on 5-line sample produced perfect match to expected output. All transformations working: column reversal, uppercasing, whitespace removal, delimiter change to semicolon, and ";OK" suffix. Exit code 0. Script is ready for full 1M row execution.
